structure_display.line: Drawn with the cobalt bonded to the four nitrogens of the ring, to the methyl group above the ring and to the benzimidazole nitrogen below it, which PubChem's one-line structure leaves apart; a flat drawing puts those two to either side. The + written on the cobalt is formal bookkeeping; the cobalt itself is cobalt(III). PubChem's record of it carries no stereochemistry; the wedges shown are those of hydroxocobalamin's record, which shares this skeleton.

why_it_matters.text: The form of vitamin B12 the body uses directly in the methylation cycle, sold as an alternative to cyanocobalamin in supplements.

parts.label: The amide group
parts.sentence: A C=O bonded to a nitrogen, the same link that joins amino acids in a protein. It is sturdy, and its nitrogen is not a base the way an amine's is.

parts.label: The phosphate group
parts.sentence: A phosphorus atom bonded to four oxygens. Living cells use phosphate groups to carry energy, as in ATP, and to switch molecules on and off.

parts.label: The hydroxyl group
parts.sentence: An O-H on a carbon that is not part of an aromatic ring, the group that makes a molecule an alcohol. It both gives and accepts hydrogen bonds, which helps the molecule mix with water.
